title: OEKO-TEX traceability gains momentum ahead of new EU rules
summary:
OEKO-TEX strengthened traceability across global textile supply chains in 2025/26, with ORGANIC COTTON certified volumes exceeding 33 million kg across more than 20 countries and certificates rising over 200 per cent.
MADE IN GREEN demand grew over 13 per cent, while digital traceability tools and independent certification support compliance with evolving EU rules.

title: India’s DGFT automates free sale certificates for exporters
summary:
India’s DGFT has enabled automated issuance of Free Sale and Commerce Certificates on its portal for eligible export applications. 
The change covers items outside the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940, reducing manual routing for many certificate requests. 
Applications needing checks will still go to regional authorities, with risk-based review retained for oversight.

title: Austria’s J. Zimmer to merge Klagenfurt, Kufstein from January 1, 2028
summary:
J. Zimmer Maschinenbau has launched ‘Zimmer 2028’, a strategic transformation that will merge its Klagenfurt and Kufstein operations into one organisation from January 1, 2028.
Thomas Mentler and Andreas Rass now lead both companies, as Zimmer aims to consolidate expertise, speed decision-making, strengthen customer support and innovation, and support long-term growth.

title: Global cotton output to slightly exceed consumption in 2026-27
summary:
Global cotton output is forecast at 26.2 million tonnes in 2026-27, just above use, though weather and pests could cut surplus. 
India’s crop and mill use are rising on textile export growth, while Pakistan’s weaker output will deepen raw cotton import reliance. 
China reserve sales aid supply, but Xinjiang risks may lift imports; US acreage and Section 301 tariffs could redirect sourcing flows.

title: Global air cargo demand rises 3.9% in July: IATA
summary:
Global air cargo demand rose 3.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in July 2026, with international operations up 4.7 per cent. 
Capacity grew more slowly at 1.7 per cent, a key planning signal for time-sensitive textile and apparel shipments. 
Asia-Pacific, Europe and North America drove over 90 per cent of growth, while fuel, geopolitics and tariff uncertainty remain risks.

title: ICE cotton corrects sharply due to profit booking, stronger dollar
summary:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled at 91.55 cents, down 1.59 cent, after gaining about 13 per cent in August. 
A stronger US dollar, improved rainfall and profit-taking pressured prices, while crude oil strength failed to support cotton. 
Open interest reached 382,071, the third-highest in cotton history; USDA rated the US crop 39 per cent Good/Excellent versus 51 per cent a year earlier.

title: UK’s VeriVide unveils UltraView60 for flexible LED colour assessment
summary:
VeriVide has launched UltraView60, a compact, lower-cost colour assessment cabinet featuring the same tuneable LED technology as the renamed UltraView90.
Designed for organisations with limited space, it supports multiple light sources, meets key international standards and offers a durable, adaptable solution as industries transition towards LED-based colour assessment.

title: 40% FOC rule could force a new MMF capacity race in Bangladesh
summary:
Bangladesh imported $1.818 billion of selected MMF fibres, yarns and fabrics in H1 2026, up 2.34 per cent year on year.
Woven MMF fabric made up 63.0 per cent of the basket, with China supplying 81.85 per cent.
The August Import Policy Order raises FOC thresholds to 40 per cent for specialised synthetic-fibre products and underwear, testing backward linkages.

title: Cook Islands' Penrhyn port upgrade to get US, New Zealand funding
summary:
US, Cook Islands and New Zealand plan a major upgrade at Penrhyn port in the northern Cook Islands.
The US intends $50 million funding and New Zealand $NZ17.5 million, with New Zealand to implement the project.
Shippers and sourcing teams may see safer landings, stronger transport links and wider economic opportunities in the northern Cook Islands.

title: Europe textile sector urges €10 handling fee on import parcels
summary:
The European textile industry has backed the EU’s €3 (~$3.49) duty on low-value imports but says stronger enforcement is needed.
It is calling for a handling fee of around €10 (~$11.63) per parcel to fund customs, product-safety checks and market surveillance, while urging greater platform accountability and tighter controls across both B2C and B2B imports.

title: US' UniFirst launches new Always U uniform collection
summary:
UniFirst launched Always U, a rental workwear line using poly/cotton mechanical-stretch fabrics and mobility features for active teams. 
It targets manufacturing, distribution, transport, technical services and trades where uniforms need durability, comfort and a professional look. 
A dedicated women's line addresses fit and movement gaps in standard workwear; shipments begin September 5, 2026.

title: US’ G-III Apparel & WHP complete acquisition of Marc Jacobs from LVMH
summary:
WHP Global and G-III have closed the acquisition of Marc Jacobs from LVMH and formed an equal-stake venture to co-own its intellectual property. 
WHP Global leads licensing; G-III runs wholesale, retail and e-commerce through the operating business and a long-term licence. 
Marc Jacobs remains founder and creative director as the partners target global growth and new market and product categories.

title: India’s garment exporters go global as US apparel trade falls 25%
summary:
TexPro says India’s apparel exports fell 11.2 per cent year on year to about $7.88 billion in H1 2026, with US shipments down 24.5 per cent.
UK, Germany, Netherlands, Spain, France and Italy raised their combined share to 34.61 per cent, though value slipped about 1.5 per cent.
Exporters are building networks across Asia, Africa and the Americas as origin optionality becomes a sourcing hedge.

title: Bangladesh businesses seek sector plans for LDC graduation
summary:
Bangladesh business leaders want sector-wise LDC graduation plans backed by reliable data, implementation tracking and stronger private-sector input.
They warned exporters may face loss of EU GSP and EBA duty-free access after graduation.
Firms were urged to improve productivity, skills, technology, finance access, trade capacity and IP readiness.

title: South Korea’s cumulative apparel imports slightly up but down in July
summary:
South Korea’s apparel imports rose 1.34 per cent to $6.617 billion in January-July 2026, Korea Customs Service data show.
Knitted apparel imports grew 3.64 per cent to $2.886 billion, while non-knitted apparel eased 0.36 per cent to $3.731 billion.
July apparel imports fell 3.93 per cent year on year; textile exports of man-made filaments and knitted fabrics also declined in January-July.

title: Apparel’s tariff map just changed; who gains the advantage?
summary:
US apparel imports fell 7.8 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, while Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam gained and China and India retreated sharply.
New Section 301 duties put Vietnam and China in a 12.5 per cent group, above the 10 per cent rate for Cambodia, India, Indonesia and others.
Qualifying CAFTA-DR and USMCA goods are exempt; August and September data will offer a cleaner test.

title: Global garment trade nears $550 bn as synthetic fibres gain share
summary:
Global knit and woven garment exports neared $550 billion in 2025, making up nearly 60 per cent of world textile exports.
China remained dominant, while Bangladesh rose to second and Vietnam to third among textile exporters.
Synthetic fibres are taking a larger share of garment growth, putting cotton quality and competitiveness higher on sourcing agendas.

title: Türkiye’s apparel exports dip 1% in Jan-Jul; July stays positive
summary:
Turkiye's apparel exports declined 1.05 per cent year on year to $9.304 billion in January-July 2026, with HS 61 at $5.387 billion and HS 62 at $3.917 billion. 
July exports under HS 61 and HS 62 rose 3.13 per cent to $1.469 billion after strong June growth. 
Recovery remains incomplete after 2025 exports fell 6.26 per cent amid weak European demand and price competition.

title: Tk 30,000 wage demand could raise Bangladesh’s SS27 risk
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment sector is entering its first minimum-wage review under a shortened three-year cycle, with unions seeking reconstitution of the Minimum Wage Board. 
The last structure took effect in December 2023, pointing to a new one by December 2026 under the amended labour law. 
RMG exports were US$39.35 billion in FY2024-25, up 8.84 per cent, with an 81.49 per cent share of total exports.

title: 26-point duty gap could favour flexible apparel sourcing
summary:
A rebuilt United States tariff structure is shifting apparel sourcing from choosing one country to moving between several quickly. 
India’s PDS Limited and Indonesia’s Busana Apparel Group have announced a non-binding alliance across six manufacturing locations. 
New Section 301 duties create a landed-cost gap that could favour CAFTA-DR apparel from Honduras and Nicaragua.
